First of all thank you for taking up the challenge!

A few things:
- We are very careful when adding new libraries, and this feature doesn't seem to need any
- We should keep it simpler as @vjeux mentioned and not use any external library
- Move the component to the [`components`](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/tree/master/src/components) directory
- For the final look and feel, we'll iterate later
- All the copy should be added to the [`en.json`](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/blob/master/src/locales/en.json) and use it like: `t("labels.copy")` for example (to be able to support other languages). Maybe a new section for these hints?

Thanks for the review @lipis. I am having problems in implementing toasts from scratch in typescript. Are there any code samples or resources you could link here so I can take a reference from there?

Thanks @rish07 for the PR!

I'm with @lipis — I don't think we should pull in half a megabyte of libs (minified) just for this one feature. CSS should be enough for this. If we stick to current implem where we don't display more than 1 toast at a time, it should be even simpler. I'm sure we'll figure it out.

Sidenotes:

- I'd not show toasts for copy/cut actions as that's pretty obvious and would be distracting as you do those actions often.
- Do we want to show toasts when the action isn't invoked via a shortcut? E.g. when I click on `copy as svg` via contextmenu, I don't think I need a toast confirmation for this.
We have a simpler toast in another PR.. so we'll close this one. Thanks for the effort. #2772

@vjeux Thanks for the quick reply. I am new to typescript and have only been a user of excalidraw but I am familiar with frontend dev in flutter. And I see this as an opportunity to learn something new. Could you help me with how to get started on this?

Toasts are fun. They can create some tricky animation problems when you have more than one on the screen at once because you need to FLIP current toasts to new their new position when older toasts disappear. See that example @lipis posted above.

We could simplify the problem by having only one toast on the screen at a time and making new toasts occlude / dismiss earlier ones. We could also have all toasts be a fixed size, which would let us animate by hand to known values without having to FLIP.

If we did want to have the whole package, we could still do the FLIP stuff ourselves without adding a library.
Are there other places in the app where we might want to toast a message? Maybe when a contributor joins, or when a project is copied / exported?
